# DSH Pets · dsh-pets-multiworkers
**One tank, every conversation — see what your AI is doing at a glance.**
Most pet plugins give you one mascot. This one puts **every active top-level conversation in the sam
e tank at once**, so a whole work queue is visible without switching sessions:
| What you need to know | How the tank shows it |
| Which conversation is working | Each pet plays its own real phase — thinking, tool running, waitin
g for you, done, failed — with that session's own status bubble. Background pets sit at 52.7% size s

o the focused one reads first. |
| Which model or vendor is busy | Stable per-session palettes for D

eepSeek, GPT, Claude, GLM, Kimi and more, plus extra hues that keep same-vendor sessions apart. |
|
How fast it is going | Left/right running speed follows that session's footer tok/s (`FPS = max(1, k

× tok/s + b)`), so a faster model visibly runs faster. |
| A conversation to keep watching | Open t
he row's `...` menu (or right-click it) → **专属宠物保持** (keep pet shown): the conversation's own pet st
ops being recycled after its result is viewed and you move on. Focus gives it the main size; the res

t stay secondary. |
| What a subagent is doing | Opening a subagent hands the main pet that session'
s own generation state and footer rate; returning restores the parent. Subagent pets keep the ordina

ry show/hide rules. |
| Desktop presence | Optional native overlay windows without patching app.asar
, a status-only bubble mode with no artwork, and a hover or right-click care panel. |
[该节后续省略]
## Installation
In **Settings → Plugins → Add plugin**, enter **`dsh-pets-multiworkers`**. The registry listing is n
ew; until the catalog index picks it up, install the Release archive or a local archive as described
below. Enter the package name instead of the GitHub repository URL to use the precompiled package a
nd avoid downloading the source archive.
Use the Desktop installation's exact CLI, rather than an older global dsh:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
For a custom installation, point $dsh to its resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh.cmd. Do not add resources
/runtime/bin to the global PATH. Download `dsh-pets-multiworkers-1.5.0.tgz`, verify SHA256SUMS.txt,
then install a named local target, replacing the example path:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Users need not pack the repository or install pnpm. Use web for a web host. First-time bundle additi
ons can hot-load. Fully quit and reopen DSH for a loaded-version replacement, restart-required recei
pt or stale client UI; successful hot-loading does not itself need a restart. Native companions use
the existing Desktop runtime without patching app.asar or installing another Node/Electron/PowerShel
ng Desktop runtime without patching app.asar or installing another Node/Electron/PowerShell runtime.
## Rename migration
Version 1.5.0 renames `dsh-pet-copilot` to `dsh-pets-multiworkers`. Back up DSH, remove the old `dsh
-pet-copilot` bundle (and any older `@ltmroberthk915/dsh-pet` / `@linxin666/dsh-pet` row) from the s
elected profile, then install the new name. Run the launcher from the Release's `dsh-pet-profile-mig
ration-1.5.0.zip` or the installed scripts directory. DSH matches overrides by both row ID and packa
ge name, so keeping only `id: pet` does not preserve settings saved under the old name.
The tool validates real Host composition, backs up the patch, and changes only matching name scalars
in one profile. Config, disabled state, comments and other plugins survive. The shared home patch i
s never rewritten. Conflicts with newer settings, aliases or concurrent edits stop the operation; a
profile that already carries more than one inert legacy pet row is stopped for review instead of pro
ducing duplicate matching rows. Care data remains in the original pet.json. See the migration guide.
## Release age and registry source
Default non-strict pnpm 11.7.0 can install a fresh release and automatically add a version-specific
exclusion. Explicit minimumReleaseAge: 1440 without disabling strict behavior rejects immature relea
ses. With minimumReleaseAgeStrict: true, exact pins and npm tarball URLs cannot bypass the threshold
. Longer custom waiting periods remain effective. Default-policy success does not prove strict-polic
y success; not every user must wait 24 hours.
For updates, publish to next, preserve the existing stable latest, wait at least 24 hours, then requ
ire a strict registry-install receipt without exclusions before promoting latest. First publication
has a separate initialization path: npm automatically creates latest and rejects removing it; staged
publishing initially points it at an empty 0.0.0-stage package. After official-registry fresh insta
llation and identical-version reinstallation pass, initialize latest to the first real release while
retaining next. The initialization command rejects packages with any earlier real published version
. Consumer global policies are never modified.
Identical-version reinstalls have a separate lockfile check. With real pnpm 11.7.0 and an isolated r
egistry, upgrading 1.3.2 to 1.3.3 succeeds, but immediately adding 1.3.3 again fails with `ERR_PNPM_
MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION` despite both version exclusions. The installed version and bundle sel
ection survive. Do not delete user lockfiles or disable global policies to mask the failure; verify
fresh installs, upgrades and reinstalls separately.
[该节后续省略]
## Development
Use pnpm 11.7.0: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `
pnpm build`, then `node scripts/build-desktop-manifest.mjs` and `node scripts/package-companions.mjs
pm build`, then `node scripts/build-desktop-manifest.mjs` and `node scripts/package-companions.mjs`.
Archives omit development source, tests and consumer lifecycle scripts, exclude retired MIKU interpo
lation frames, and are reopened to validate all served assets and JavaScript entries. Migration test
s use actual loadProfileDirectory and composeEntries; release-age tests isolate profiles, caches and
stores and use the official manager and market bridge. Fixture-registry, public-registry and catalo
g results are distinct. See the Windows guide.
